judgements.reason: Semisimple algebras is essentially complete in Tau Ceti (Wedderburn invariants and uniqueness, density theorem, Skolem-Noether, centralizer theorem, Brauer group with base change, index and Br(R) = Z/2), leaving at most worked examples; effective bounds still lacks explicit lower bounds for the regulator in positive unit rank. Both residuals are small.

Analytic toric geometry still needs Minkowski-Weyl and Gordan's lemma, affine toric schemes and fan gluing, regular analytic charts with a complex-manifold gluing theorem, the orbit-cone correspondence and SNC boundary, the properness criterion and the algebraic-analytic comparison; effective bounds only lacks positive-rank regulator lower bounds.

Toric geometry's missing theory is broad but shallow (cone lemmas, toric schemes and gluing, manifold charts and gluing, orbits and boundary, properness, comparison). Chebotarev needs a deeper analytic stack: power-saving ray-class ideal counts over Lipschitz-parametrized fundamental domains, ray-class characters with L-series continuation and nonvanishing, the unsmoothed Wiener-Ikehara theorem and prime ideal theorem, then the Dirichlet-density calculus and the abelian, general and weighted crossings.

Chebotarev's gap is classical analytic number theory over number fields (ray-class counts, L-series near Re s = 1, Wiener-Ikehara, density crossings) on a largely built algebraic half. Additive combinatorics needs the prime number theorem, zero-density estimates and Bombieri-Vinogradov, then Freiman/BSG, Szemeredi's theorem, Gowers norms with the Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem and nilmanifold equidistribution, the Green-Tao theorem and linear equations in primes.

Additive combinatorics needs a tall analytic tower (PNT, zero-density and Bombieri-Vinogradov; Freiman/BSG, Szemeredi, the GTZ inverse theorem with nilsequences, Green-Tao, linear equations in primes). Drinfeld modules has almost nothing built and needs algebraic stacks, etale base change, Picard schemes and deformation theory (SF.1-SF.4) and function-field adeles beneath nine deep layers: C_infinity uniformization, moduli with Pink's compactification, t-motives, the Taguchi-Tamagawa Tate conjecture, Taelman's class-number formula, elliptic sheaves and Papanikolas' Tannakian transcendence.

Drinfeld modules needs stack and etale foundations plus its nine Drinfeld-module layers. Q-series imports much more: metaplectic automorphic forms MP.0-MP.8 with automorphic spectral theory, the Weil bounds through ES.3/FF.2 (Weil conjectures, Deligne purity, Lefschetz pencils, etale duality), WRT invariants QT.0-QT.4 and Habiro completions, on top of its own harmonic Maass forms, Zwegers completions and the whole moonshine proof (vertex algebras, moonshine module, no-ghost theorem, Borcherds).

(phi,Gamma)-modules needs Fontaine's equivalence, Cherbonnier-Colmez, Herr and psi complexes, Wach modules and KPX families on imports of local Tate duality, period rings, perfectoid P0-P3 and Iwasawa algebras (about 48 stages). Q-series imports about 130 stages, including metaplectic automorphic forms, the Weil conjectures and Deligne purity via the Weil bounds and WRT invariants, and must also build mock modular forms and moonshine.

Habiro rings imports infinity-categories and spectra, derived de Rham, prismatic cohomology including q-crystalline PR.6, q-Hodge cohomology HQ.1-HQ.5, and through HB.7 the whole K-theory stack with the norm-residue theorem, before its own E-infinity cyclotomic descent and q-Witt constructions. (phi,Gamma)-modules needs p-adic period rings, local duality and Iwasawa algebras beneath a chain of local layers (Fontaine, overconvergence, Herr, psi, Wach, KPX).

Both import the K-theory stack (norm residue, Quillen-Lichtenbaum), infinity-categorical foundations and perfectoid P0-P3. Beyond that Habiro rings adds prismatic and derived de Rham cohomology, HQ.1-HQ.5 and its Habiro constructions, while Iwasawa theory adds far more: modular curves, Kubota-Leopoldt and Deligne-Ribet p-adic L-functions, Coleman power series, Birch-Tate and complex comparison, plus its own Mazur-Wiles, Wiles, Dasgupta-Kakde, Kurihara and Ferrero-Washington proofs.

Perfectoid quotients needs infinity-categorical derived algebra, cotangent complex and derived de Rham, crystalline and prismatic cohomology with Hodge-Tate comparison, almost purity, then universal prisms and Andre's lemma. Iwasawa theory's closure already contains many of those foundations (E0-E3 and E5, CR.0-CR.2 and CR.4, perfectoid P0-P3) and adds the K-theory stack with the norm-residue theorem, modular curves, p-adic L-functions, Iwasawa algebras and several main-conjecture proofs.

Completed cohomology's closure contains all of perfectoid quotients (through A_inf cohomology and relative Fargues-Fontaine, for the p-adic Hodge comparison of automorphic Galois representations) and adds etale cohomology with Weil II, Shimura curves and compactifications, GL2 automorphic representations and Jacquet-Langlands, automorphic Galois representations, (phi,Gamma)-modules and p-adic local Langlands for GL2(Qp), and Emerton's local-global compatibility.

The two share perfectoid, diamond, A_inf, crystalline and derived de Rham foundations (about 92 stages). Habiro cohomology adds q-de Rham, q-Hodge and q-Witt theory with spectra, THH and HR.1-HR.4 (about 34 stages), whereas completed cohomology adds about 290: etale cohomology and Weil II, Shimura varieties and compactifications, diamond six operations, p-adic local Langlands, GL2 transfer and the trace formula, completed cohomology and Emerton's theorem.

Habiro cohomology's gap is q-Hodge and q-Witt theory on prismatic, A_inf, perfectoid and infinity-categorical foundations. Modularity and Langlands extensions applies the whole potential-automorphy infrastructure (Igusa varieties, torsion Galois representations, patching, Shimura varieties, Weil II, p-adic Hodge theory) and the invariant trace formula, then must build Newton-Thorne symmetric powers and Arthur's endoscopic classification with the fundamental lemma.

Semisimple algebras is essentially fully built in Tau Ceti, from the Wedderburn invariants to Br(R) = Z/2. Analytic toric geometry still lacks dual semigroups and Gordan's lemma, toric schemes and fan gluing, analytic charts with manifold gluing, the orbit-cone correspondence and SNC boundary, properness and the algebraic-analytic comparison.

(phi,Gamma)-modules is a local p-adic Hodge chain (Fontaine equivalence, overconvergence, Herr and psi complexes, Wach modules, KPX) on about 48 imported stages. Modularity and Langlands extensions needs the potential-automorphy infrastructure, the trace formula, endoscopic classification and symmetric-power functoriality on about 400 imported stages that include p-adic Hodge theory itself.

Semisimple algebras has no substantive missing layer in the baseline. Chebotarev still needs power-saving ray-class ideal counts, ray-class L-series continuation and nonvanishing, the unsmoothed Wiener-Ikehara theorem, the prime ideal theorem and every Dirichlet- and natural-density theorem.

Habiro cohomology's comparison atlas HQ.8 imports all of perfectoid quotients, and even its core HQ.1-HQ.5 needs more than PQ's imports: the q-crystalline and AOmega comparison PR.6, A_inf cohomology AI.1-AI.4, de Rham-Witt CR.4-CR.5, derived de Rham DD.3-DD.6, spectra and THH, and Habiro rings HR.1-HR.4, before its q-Hodge filtrations and q-Witt descent. Relative to that core, perfectoid quotients adds only derived adic completion E4, perfectoid morphisms P4 and its own universal prisms, Andre's lemma and perfectoidization surjectivity.

Q-series imports the Weil conjectures and Deligne purity (via the Weil bounds), Vinogradov mean values, metaplectic automorphic forms and WRT invariants, and must build moonshine and mock modular forms. Iwasawa theory imports a larger stack, the whole K-theory development with the norm-residue theorem and Quillen-Lichtenbaum, p-adic L-functions via Hilbert Eisenstein series, Iwasawa algebras, Coleman power series and Birch-Tate, and must build several main-conjecture proofs (Mazur-Wiles, Wiles, Dasgupta-Kakde, Kurihara).

The potential-automorphy infrastructure that ML.2 applies shares about 313 stages with completed cohomology's closure (Shimura varieties, etale cohomology, p-adic Hodge theory, perfectoid geometry). Completed cohomology adds GL2-specific modular curves, p-adic local Langlands and Emerton's theorem, while modularity and Langlands adds Igusa varieties, torsion Galois representations and patching, plus Arthur's classification with the fundamental lemma and Newton-Thorne symmetric powers.

Drinfeld modules needs stack and etale foundations (SF.1-SF.4) under its nine Drinfeld-module layers. Habiro rings needs a far larger imported closure: infinity-categories and spectra, derived de Rham, prismatic and A_inf cohomology, q-Hodge cohomology HQ.1-HQ.5, and the K-theory stack with Bloch groups, Borel regulators and the norm-residue theorem, before its own Habiro constructions.

Additive combinatorics needs PNT, zero-density and Bombieri-Vinogradov and a tall analytic tower (Freiman/BSG, Szemeredi, the GTZ inverse theorem and nilsequences, Green-Tao, linear equations in primes) on measure-theoretic and Fourier foundations that Mathlib largely has. Perfectoid quotients needs more stacked foundations absent from both libraries: infinity-categorical derived sheaves and animated rings, cotangent complex and derived de Rham, crystalline and prismatic cohomology with Hodge-Tate comparison, perfectoid spaces with almost purity, then universal prisms and Andre's lemma.

Effective bounds only lacks positive-rank regulator lower bounds. Chebotarev still needs its analytic spine (power-saving ray-class counts, ray-class characters, L-series continuation and nonvanishing, Wiener-Ikehara, the prime ideal theorem) and every density theorem.

Drinfeld modules needs stack and etale foundations and its own Drinfeld-module layers. Habiro cohomology needs infinity-categorical, derived de Rham, crystalline and de Rham-Witt, prismatic, A_inf, perfectoid, diamond and relative Fargues-Fontaine theory plus spectra, THH and Habiro rings before its q-de Rham, q-Hodge and q-Witt layers.

Iwasawa theory's unique imports are the K-theory stack (norm residue, Quillen-Lichtenbaum, Borel), used for its K-theoretic comparison, plus p-adic L-functions, Coleman power series and Birch-Tate, with several main-conjecture proofs of its own. Completed cohomology's imports on its critical path are larger: etale cohomology with Weil II for Shimura curves, Shimura compactifications, GL2 automorphic representations and the trace formula, p-adic comparison via A_inf and perfectoid/diamond geometry, (phi,Gamma)-modules and p-adic local Langlands, then completed cohomology and Emerton's theorem.
